incident-bot: ALERT: prod/inference-api p99 latency > 3s and 5xx rate rising. auto-paging oncall. dashboard: https://graf.redwood/prod/inference-api/alerts/1778880000
Alice M: oncall here, I'm seeing the alert. anyone who touched canary this morning?
Ben G: I pushed canary at 10:52 (canary-2026-03-15), changed connection pool TTL + keepalive. rolled to 10% at 10:52. health green until ~11:06 then spike.
Carla R: gateway showing surge of 504/502. traces point to inference-runtime tail latency. backend spans with "read timeout" and long socket wait.
Dave L: adding eng-runtime. @Erin S paging — can you take lead?
Erin S: on it. digging into runtime logs: repeating "read timeout after 15s" from runtime->model-worker connections. looks like sockets not being reused, lots of new connects.
deploy-bot: deploy canary-2026-03-15 by Ben G at 10:52 (10% traffic)
Alice M: do we have circuit-breakers or automatic canary throttles?
Carla R: gateway retries amplified the problem — clients retried quickly, queue depth jumped. request queue p99 went 120ms -> 1.8s.
Ben G: the pool TTL change causes earlier drops of idle conns, so under burst we create more new TLS handshakes. wasn't obvious in local testing.
Erin S: proposed immediate mitigations:
• pause/rollback canary
• set gateway retry-policy=fail-fast
• temporarily scale up runtime replicas
Alice M: agree. Ben, can you rollback now? I'll shift traffic and coordinate comms.
Ben G: rolling back now:
```bash
redwood deploy rollback --target canary-2026-03-15 --confirm
# fallback: kubectl -n inference rollout undo deployment/serving-runtime
```
deploy-bot: rollback initiated for canary-2026-03-15 by Ben G
Erin S: I'm increasing replica count from 8 -> 12 to absorb pressure, and adding a short iptable SO_REUSEADDR tweak on a subset for testing.
Carla R: applying gateway fail-fast: `redwood routing update --service inference-api --retry-policy fail-fast` — reduces retry amplification.
Alice M: shifting traffic 100% back to stable-2026-03-01 and doing warmup hits to avoid cold-start cliffs.
Ben G: rollback completed, canary removed at 11:12.
deploy-bot: rollback completed for canary-2026-03-15
incident-bot: METRIC: p99 dropped from 3.6s -> 0.38s within 6m after rollback.
Carla R: 5xx rate down from 4.1% -> 0.2%.
Alice M: quick impact estimate: query shows ~1.1M requests in spike window (11:05-11:14), ~68k 5xx/timeouts. customers heavily hit: A-102, B-241.
Dave L: tagging affected accounts and internal teams. will draft customer note.
Erin S: root cause hypothesis: pool TTL reduction -> more new connections -> kernel fd churn / TLS handshake latencies on a subset of nodes. gateway retries caused cascading queueing and tail latency.
Ben G: able to reproduce with traffic replay: new-connection-heavy workload increases p99 x3.
Carla R: follow-ups: create postmortem ticket PM-4521. runtime fix to harden new-connection path + add socket reuse metrics. owning postmortem + follow-up.
Ben G: I'll prepare a safer pool config and change canary rollout steps (2% -> 5% -> 10%) with longer observation. also add integration test for connection churn.
Erin S: will add kernel fd / socket metrics and a small perf patch; ETA EOD for dashboards.
oncall-sre: handover: I'll monitor for 2 hours; if p99 > 1s reopen paging. handing off post-incident to @Carla R for follow-up.
incident-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED: Major - recovered. Alert auto-closed at 11:28. Please file postmortem within 72h.
Alice M: logs: `grep \"read timeout\" /var/log/runtime/*.log | wc -l` -> ~68k hits during window.
Ben G: postmortem notes: increase canary dwell, add traffic-shaping test, avoid aggressive pool TTL churn.
Carla R: PM-4521 created and assigned to eng-runtime + eng-sre; will post link here.
Dave L: customer email draft ETA 90m, will include numbers and remediation plan. recommend SLA credit discussion.
Erin S: reverting fail-fast retry and scaling down nodes after monitoring window; will coordinate schedule with SRE.
Alice M: marking thread resolved; will watch for 1h then remove. :thumbsup: reactions from many.
